title: School network reorganization under educational and spatial constraints using classical and quantum optimization
authors: Alessia Ciacco, Luigi Di Puglia Pugliese, Francesca Guerriero
abstract: School network reorganization is a strategic planning problem that requires balancing demographic trends, territorial accessibility, educational requirements, and institutional constraints while ensuring an efficient allocation of public resources. This paper proposes an optimization framework for school dimensioning decisions based on a novel Integer Linear Programming formulation integrating geographical, administrative, and educational criteria. A synthetic benchmark generator is introduced to evaluate the scalability and computational performance of the model on artificial instances, while a real-world case study involving the complete public school network of the Calabria region (Italy) is conducted using actual institutional, territorial, and demographic data. The proposed approach effectively identifies optimal aggregation plans under different policy scenarios while preserving the structural characteristics of the educational system. Furthermore, the model is reformulated as a constrained quadratic model and implemented within a hybrid quantum optimization environment, demonstrating its compatibility with emerging quantum technologies. The results highlight the robustness of the proposed methodology and its potential as a decision-support tool for sustainable and equitable school network planning.
summary: This paper proposes an advanced mathematical framework using Integer Linear Programming to solve the complex problem of reorganizing public school networks. It applies this model to real Italian data, comparing classical computational results against those obtained from hybrid quantum optimization environments. The work establishes a robust decision-support tool for sustainable and equitable resource allocation in educational infrastructure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the strategic planning problem of school network reorganization, aiming to efficiently allocate public resources while balancing demographic trends, accessibility, and educational requirements.
main_result: The proposed optimization framework effectively identifies optimal aggregation plans for real-world regions like Calabria, demonstrating its potential as a robust decision-support tool for equitable infrastructure planning.
method: It develops an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation that is also reformulated as a constrained quadratic model, allowing it to be implemented and tested within a hybrid quantum optimization environment alongside classical solvers.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the public school network of a region (e.g., Calabria), which must be partitioned into optimal clusters based on complex constraints including travel time, capacity, and administrative compatibility.
key_observables: Optimal aggregation plans, objective function values ($z_C$ vs $z_Q$), structural indicators ($	ext{CZ}, 	ext{KR}, 	ext{RC}$, etc.), and solution times for various policy scenarios.
important_parameters: Policy configurations (64 tested), maximum execution time limits ($T_{IC}^{max} = 1200 	ext{ s}$), and integration of multiple constraints like territorial criticality and accessibility.
main_assumptions: The methodology assumes that the problem can be accurately modeled by integrating geographical, administrative, and educational criteria into a single optimization framework; quantum performance is noted as potentially limited by current hardware capabilities.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables comparing classical vs. quantum objective values and solution times across policy configurations for the Calabria case study.
paper_structure: The paper systematically reviews related literature on facility planning, details its novel ILP/quadratic formulation integrating multiple constraints, applies this framework to a real-world Italian case study (Calabria), and compares classical optimization results with preliminary quantum annealing results.
why_interesting: While the core problem is civil engineering/operations research, the explicit reformulation into a constrained quadratic model and subsequent testing on Quantum Annealing environments makes it relevant for demonstrating near-term applications of quantum computation to complex combinatorial optimization problems.
